Confirmed this is a regression. Tested across versions:

- **1.14.21**: `/exit` and Ctrl+C both exit cleanly, pwsh stays alive ✓
- **1.15.6**: `/exit` and Ctrl+C kill the parent process ✗

Consistent with #25677 which reports the same regression starting from 1.14.25. Rolling back to 1.14.21 (via scoop) is a working workaround on Windows.

This issue has been automatically closed because it was not updated to meet our [contributing guidelines](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md) within the 2-hour window.

Feel free to open a new issue that follows our issue templates.

Bisected this down to the exact commit: **`4877ecc`** (PR [#24215](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/24215) — "Fix shell cwd after login startup").

- **1.14.24 (before the PR)**: `/exit` and Ctrl+C exit cleanly, shell stays alive ✓
- **1.14.25 (after the PR)**: `/exit` and Ctrl+C kill the parent terminal/process ✗

The PR changed `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` — refactored how the working directory is passed to shell commands (from `$PWD` capture to `$1` positional parameter). This altered the shell process invocation signature for zsh/bash, and appears to have a side effect on how opencode spawns/terminates the TUI shell process on Windows, causing the parent terminal process to be killed when exiting via `/exit` or Ctrl+C.

**Update: Found the actual root cause, not PR #24215.**

The real change that introduced this regression is the **OpenTUI version bump** in v1.14.25:

| Dependency | v1.14.24 (working) | v1.14.25 (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| `@opentui/core` | 0.1.99 | **0.1.103** |
| `@opentui/solid` | 0.1.99 | **0.1.103** |

PR #24215 (shell cwd fix) was coincidental — the OpenTUI bump from 0.1.99 to 0.1.103 changed how the TUI process terminates on Windows, causing the parent terminal process to be killed on `/exit` and Ctrl+C. This aligns with @Hona's earlier comment about it being a bun-level issue.

The move from pinned versions (`"0.1.99"`) to workspace catalog references (`"catalog:"`) in packages/opencode/package.json is what allowed this version jump to land unnoticed.

If the real symptom is just "double-click exe, nothing happens," then the next split should be as low-friction as possible:

1. **Did the process start and crash, or never start at all?**
   - Open Task Manager, double-click `OpenCode.exe`, and see whether a process appears briefly.
2. **Did Windows log an application error?**
   - Event Viewer -> Windows Logs -> Application
   - look for an Error entry around the exact launch time with `OpenCode.exe` or a DLL/runtime name
3. **Can the binary say *anything* from a terminal?**
   - open `cmd.exe`
   - run the installed exe from its folder, or run `opencode --version` if the CLI is on PATH

That gives maintainers a very different direction depending on the result:
- process never appears -> launcher / packaging boundary
- process flashes then dies with an Application Error -> native crash / dependency boundary
- terminal prints an error -> bootstrap/config boundary

The reason I am pushing that split is the downgrade anecdote above: that sounds more like a startup-path regression than a user config problem, and the fastest way to prove that is one event-log entry or one terminal error line.

I am sorry to be a pedantic passerby that comment freely while not contributing (I am), but as useful as what is proposed here can be (token consumption will be the main differentiator between code harnesses in the coming times of rising token costs) it is not exactly the same ideas as what Dirac does.|

The whole Dirac anchor process is explained here : https://dirac.run/posts/hash-anchors-myers-diff-single-token

Basically :
* The anchor does not depend on the context they are not hashes.
* They do not need to be recomputed "willy nilly" depending on changes surrounding the insertion point.
* Avoiding round trip to the LLM is the point, so avoiding invalid anchors is paramount.
* They use a neat trick for anchors : they are not ashes but a token picked from a pre made list of token to minimize input and output token consumption for hashes.

Again, I am sure this patch is useful  but this is not the same as what Dirac does and if the author is interested in this topic there might be room to milk more efficiency in token and compute.

The goal of this post is to avoid a "subject closed" when there might be room to revisit, and sorry if it comes as a lazy critic, it is, but no ill intend.

I took a quick look at current `main` to separate this from the older general Zod v3/v4 reports.

The likely useful split is **where the raw Zod object first enters the tool pipeline**, not the Kimi provider adapter itself:

- Built-in opencode tools are converted through `packages/opencode/src/tool/json-schema.ts` (`ToolJsonSchema.fromTool()` / Effect `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument`).
- Plugin Zod tools now go through `packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts` via `z.toJSONSchema(...)` and `normalizeZodJsonSchema(...)`.
- MCP tools are normalized in `packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts` with `asSchema(item.inputSchema).jsonSchema`, then passed through `ProviderTransform.schema(...)`.
- `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` already has a Kimi/Moonshot sanitizer, but it assumes the input is already JSON Schema. It strips/adjusts `$ref` siblings and tuple `items`; it does not and probably should not try to interpret raw Zod internals.

So I would add the regression/guard one layer earlier: right before `jsonSchema(transformed)` in `session/tools.ts` and for plugin tools after registry load, assert that the final schema tree contains none of `_def`, `def`, `_zod`, `~standard`, `_cached`, or `typeName`. If that guard fails, log the tool name/source (`ctx_batch_execute` / context-mode) and fail with a local diagnostic before the provider request is built.

That should answer whether this is still the known Zod conversion bug or a distinct bypass in the context-mode/MCP tool path. For Kimi specifically, a focused failing test would create a synthetic tool with an array-of-object parameter, run it through `SessionTools.resolve` for `providerID: "moonshotai"` or a Kimi model id, and assert the final AI SDK tool schema is:

```json
{
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }
}
```

with no Zod-private keys anywhere in the serialized body.

# v1.15.7 does not resolve this regression — analysis of what was actually shipped

Confirming on desktop and CLI: the `auth login` menu in **v1.15.7** still has no OpenAI / ChatGPT (browser / headless / device-code) options. The regression that landed in 1.14.49 persists.

The release notes for v1.15.7 include the line **"Restored native OpenAI OAuth requests."**, which sounds like it should fix this issue — but reading the actual diff (`v1.15.6...v1.15.7`) shows it does not. This comment is a breakdown of what changed and what is still missing, so the gap is visible to maintainers rather than hidden by the release wording.

## TL;DR

Two relevant PRs landed in v1.15.7:

| PR | Title | What it actually does | Does it fix this issue? |
|----|-------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| #28571 | `fix(opencode): support native OpenAI OAuth fetch` | Restores **runtime use** of an OpenAI OAuth token (native fetch path in `session/llm/native-runtime.ts` + `protocols/openai-responses.ts`) | ❌ No — it only matters **after** a token is already in `auth.json`. It does not restore the login flow that produces that token. |
| #28260 | `Rename v2 auth service to account` | Deletes `packages/core/src/auth.ts` (-264 lines) and `packages/core/src/plugin/auth.ts` (-27 lines); auth storage is now `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` again (not `auth-v2.json`); no `migrate()` function remains. | ❌ No — and removes the AuthV2 bridge entirely without adding OAuth registration to provider plugins. |

The original bug is in the **login flow**, not the request path: `opencode auth login` shows no OpenAI option because the OpenAI plugin does not register any OAuth methods.

## Evidence: OpenAI plugin in v1.15.7 still registers zero auth hooks

Full contents of `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/openai.ts` at tag `v1.15.7`:

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"
import { ModelV2 } from "../../model"
import { PluginV2 } from "../../plugin"
import { ProviderV2 } from "../../provider"

export const OpenAIPlugin = PluginV2.define({
  id: PluginV2.ID.make("openai"),
  effect: Effect.gen(function* () {
    return {
      "aisdk.sdk": Effect.fn(function* (evt) {
        if (evt.package !== "@ai-sdk/openai") return
        const mod = yield* Effect.promise(() => import("@ai-sdk/openai"))
        evt.sdk = mod.createOpenAI(evt.options)
      }),
      "aisdk.language": Effect.fn(function* (evt) {
        if (evt.model.providerID !== ProviderV2.ID.openai) return
        evt.language = evt.sdk.responses(evt.model.apiID)
      }),
      "catalog.transform": Effect.fn(function* (evt) {
        // ...hides gpt-5-chat-latest from OpenAI catalog
      }),
    }
  }),
})
```

Only three hooks: `aisdk.sdk`, `aisdk.language`, `catalog.transform`. None of `auth.method` / `oauth.authorize` / `oauth.callback` / equivalent are registered, which is why the `opencode auth login` menu lists no OpenAI entries at all (browser, headless, or device-code).

The new provider-auth schema lives in `packages/opencode/src/provider/auth.ts` (`Method` / `Methods` / `Authorization` / `CallbackInput` etc.) and is wired through plugin hooks — but for OpenAI, no plugin is wiring anything in, so the menu stays empty.

## Evidence: PR #28571 only touches runtime, not login

Files changed in `facd2073` (`fix(opencode): support native OpenAI OAuth fetch`):

- `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts` (3 lines)
- `packages/llm/src/protocols/utils/openai-options.ts` (5 lines)
- `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts` (2 lines)
- `packages/opencode/src/session/llm/native-runtime.ts` (59 lines)
- `packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts` (2 lines)
- tests + a recording fixture `native-openai-oauth-tool-loop.json`

# Important follow-up: runtime token reuse is ALSO broken in v1.15.7, not just the login menu

Quick correction / extension to my previous comment — based on direct testing of an upgrade path from a working 1.14.48 install, the PR #28571 "Restored native OpenAI OAuth requests" fix is **also not working** in practice. So the regression in v1.15.7 has two layers, not one:

## Layer 1 — login flow (covered in the previous comment)

`opencode auth login` menu has no OpenAI / ChatGPT options because `OpenAIPlugin` registers no auth hooks. New users cannot obtain an OAuth token at all.

## Layer 2 — runtime token reuse (this comment)

For users who **already have a working OAuth token** in `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` from 1.14.48:

- **On 1.14.48**: GPT requests work — the stored OAuth token is read and used.
- **After upgrading to 1.15.7, with the same `auth.json` file untouched, the provider never disabled and auth never changed**: opencode immediately prompts for an API Key on the first GPT request, as if the stored OAuth token did not exist.

This is the exact scenario PR #28571 (`fix(opencode): support native OpenAI OAuth fetch`) was supposed to fix — using a stored OAuth token via native fetch in the request path. But empirically, post-upgrade, opencode behaves as if it cannot read or recognize the stored OAuth credential and falls back to demanding an API key.

So the situation in v1.15.7 is:

| User state on 1.14.48 | After upgrade to 1.15.7 | Outcome |
|------------------------|------------------------|---------|
| Has OAuth token in `auth.json`, GPT requests working | Same file, same provider config | Asks for API Key — token not used |
| No token yet, wants to log in via `auth login` | Tries `auth login` | Menu has no OpenAI option — can't log in |

Either path is blocked.

## What this means

Even the runtime part of the claimed v1.15.7 fix doesn't reach end-users. This isn't only "needs new login flow" — even users who had a working setup on 1.14.48 lose the integration on upgrade. There's no current path to GPT via OAuth on v1.15.7 at all, for either new or existing users.

I haven't traced exactly where the new `auth.json` reader (`packages/opencode/src/auth/index.ts`) diverges from the previous behavior — possibly the `Oauth` schema's strict-decode rejects the 1.14.48-shaped record, possibly the provider runtime never consults `Auth.get("openai")` before falling back to API Key prompt. Either way, the symptom is reproducible: working 1.14.48 install → upgrade → API Key prompt on first request.

Adding this to the tracker so the runtime regression is on record alongside the login-menu regression.

# Root cause confirmed — `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=true` was set

Thanks for the pointer — checking my environment, **`OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=true` was indeed set as a persistent User-scope env var** on Windows. I have no recollection of setting it deliberately; it survived from some earlier debugging attempt and silently stayed in `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS","User")`.

After unsetting it, upgrading to v1.15.7, and aligning `@opencode-ai/plugin` to `1.15.7` in `~/.config/opencode/package.json`:

- `opencode auth login` now lists OpenAI with `browser` / `headless` / `device-code` options as expected
- `opencode auth list` shows `OpenAI [oauth]` and uses the stored token on requests (no API Key prompt)
- Both `auth list` and version startup are sub-1.5s with the full plugin set loaded

So the regression for me reduces to: a stale env var override.

## Behavior change worth flagging anyway

The same env var was harmless on **v1.14.48** in my setup — OpenAI OAuth (and the `auth login` menu entries for it) worked fine even with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=true`. From the diff between 1.14.48 and 1.14.49+, this lines up with the refactor that moved OAuth method registration out of the provider directly and into a default plugin. After that refactor the env var stopped being a no-op for OAuth and started gating the entire login flow for any provider whose auth methods live in a default plugin.

That's a legitimate consequence of the refactor (the env var does what it says — disables default plugins), but it surfaces as "OpenAI is silently missing from the menu" rather than something users can self-diagnose. My previous two comments here attributed this to plugin code in v1.15.7, which was the wrong root cause — apologies for the noise.

## Small UX suggestion

If `auth login` is rendered and an env var like `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS` is active, a one-line hint above the provider list would have saved a lot of investigation — something like:

```
note: OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS is set; some auth methods (incl. OpenAI/ChatGPT OAuth) are disabled
```

Same idea for `auth list` showing a warning footer when the env var is set. Cheap to add, eliminates the entire class of "menu is empty, why?" reports going forward.
